content: After activation, a waiting period of seven minutes is required before retrieving the containers. The door to the treated cargo hold should only be opened minimally for retrieval of used containers and must be immediately closed afterward to prevent recontamination. Any deviation from these procedures must be reported to the first intended port of arrival prior to reaching the destination. Contracting States to the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) are responsible for ensuring compliance with ICAO Standards and Recommended Practices outlined in Annex 9. Guidance for these procedures is available in the ICAO Facilitation Manual. When both residual and aerosol disinsection treatments are applied to an aircraft, the relevant ICAO Annex 9 documentation must be completed. Copies of the ICAO residual disinsection certificate and the General Declaration are included as annexes in the provided documentation. Upon arrival, authorities may require all exterior doors and windows, including cargo hold doors, to remain closed until permission is granted to open them. Residual treatment of the cabin and cargo hold should be conducted together. Section 6 provides detailed instructions for estimating the amount of residual spray required for different aircraft types. Any non-compliance with disinsection procedures during the flight must be reported before arrival. Residual treatment must be performed at intervals not exceeding eight weeks and can be completed whenever the aircraft is available. The recommended formulation for residual spraying is 2% permethrin emulsifiable concentrate (EC), applied at a liquid volume of ≤10 mL/m². For areas such as the flight deck, cockpit, and crew rest areas, where emulsions may cause damage or safety concerns, a 2% permethrin aerosol formulation should be used. The aircraft should be set to ground service mode before spraying. Preparation for residual cabin treatment involves opening, clearing, and cleaning all lockers, cupboards, and storage units, closing curtains and window blinds, and removing carpet covers. The air-conditioning system, including preconditioned air from ground support units, must be turned off. Recirculation fans may remain on if essential for aircraft operation but should be set to the lowest flow rate. All surfaces, including floors, ceilings, walls, lockers, curtains, toilets, and galley areas, must be sprayed. Doors and locker lids must be sprayed on both sides, and floor areas should be resprayed. Care must be taken to avoid spraying food preparation areas, seats, mirrors, windows, medical equipment, and other sensitive areas. Any accidental spray on these surfaces must be immediately wiped clean, and food-contact areas should be further cleaned with soap and water. For cargo hold disinsection, all cargo, pallets, containers, and debris must be removed before spraying. The walls, ceilings, floors, dividing curtains, and door interiors must be sprayed, with particular attention to sidewall and floor cavities. Sensitive electronic equipment should not be directly sprayed, and the crew must be informed of the procedures beforehand. Aerosols containing 2% permethrin or 2% d-phenothrin (or 1R-trans-phenothrin) may be used, depending on the authorization of the destination country. During and for five minutes after spraying, the aircraft’s air-conditioning system must remain off, and recirculation fans, if essential, should be set to the lowest flow rate. Certification of residual treatment is the responsibility of ICAO Contracting States, ensuring that aviation stakeholders implement ICAO Annex 9 standards. Templates for certification are available in the ICAO Facilitation Manual. When both residual and aerosol treatments are applied, both ICAO Annex 9 documents must be completed. Copies of the residual disinsection certificate and General Declaration are provided in the annexes. Localized or frequent cleaning of large surface areas may compromise the effectiveness of residual insecticides. If this occurs, supplementary aerosol applications may be necessary. After residual spray application, areas undergoing additional cleaning, such as wall linings and carpets, should receive a “top-up” aerosol spray containing 2% permethrin. Replacement fixtures, such as walls or carpets, must also be treated either off the aircraft or shortly after disinsection to maintain certification compliance. On-arrival disinsection procedures require all exterior doors and windows to remain closed until directed otherwise by local authorities. Passengers with medical conditions that may be affected by spraying should notify the crew, who will inform local authorities to determine if disembarkation before spraying is possible. Cabin crew must prepare the cabin by opening all overhead lockers and ensuring passengers remain seated. During spraying and for five minutes afterward, the air-conditioning system must remain off, with recirculation fans set to the lowest flow rate if necessary. Spraying should be conducted systematically, ensuring even coverage of all areas, including galleys, toilets, and crew rest areas, while avoiding sensitive equipment and surfaces. For freighter aircraft, the main entry door must remain closed during cabin spraying. Aerosols containing 2% d-phenothrin or 1R-trans-phenothrin should be used, with all overhead and sidewall lockers open during spraying. The spray must be directed toward open lockers and ceilings, ensuring even coverage. Cargo areas on the main deck should be accessed via the passenger access door, with the large cargo door remaining closed. Aerosols should be discharged as high as possible, directed toward the center of the aircraft ceiling, and evenly distributed if cargo obstructs access to certain areas. Residual spray amounts required for aircraft disinsection depend on the internal area of the aircraft. Calculations should be recorded in the operator’s manual for staff conducting spraying. Additional allowances should be made for inconsistencies in spraying, with a 33% increase added to calculated amounts.
